title: Christ Covenant Church Session v. Central Carolina Presbytery
disposition_detail: Sole issue: whether the case is judicially in order. The SJC answered no and held the case not judicially in order because H's complaint to the Session was untimely under BCO 43-2; the Session should not have received it. The SJC made no merits ruling on Presbytery's annulment or due-process findings.
first_summary: Christ Covenant Church Session complained that Central Carolina Presbytery improperly annulled the session trial commission's judgment and found due-process violations concerning H. The SJC held the case not judicially in order because H's complaint to the Session was untimely under BCO 43-2. The merits of Presbytery's action were therefore not reached.
summary: Christ Covenant Church Session complained under BCO 43 that Central Carolina Presbytery wrongly annulled the session trial commission's judgment and found due-process error concerning H. The SJC did not reach the merits. It held the case not judicially in order because H's complaint to the Session was untimely: it exceeded the thirty-day requirement of BCO 43-2 and came more than eighty days after the oral verdict. The ruling thus turned on a procedural gate, making no merits ruling on Presbytery's annulment or its due-process rationale.

evidence_notes.identity_and_adoption: Lines 1–5 identify case 2001-32, SJC, 31st GA (2003), with disposition not judicially in order. Line 54 says TE Robert D. Stuart wrote the Summary, Issues, Judgment, and Reasoning, and the full SJC amended the Reasoning and Opinion.
evidence_notes.dispute: Lines 18–35 (pp. 107–108) summarize the marriage, the Session trial of W, H's March 30, 2000 complaint to the Session, the Session's denial, H's complaint to Presbytery, and Presbytery's July 21, 2001 approval of the PC2 report annulling the trial judgment and finding due-process error under BCO 31-2. Lines 35–38 show the Session's BCO 43 complaint to the PCA.
evidence_notes.outcomes_and_reasons: Lines 42–54 (p. 109): the sole issue is whether the case is judicially in order; the judgment is No; the adopted reasoning is that the Session should not have received H's complaint because it was not timely filed under BCO 43-2's thirty-day requirement.
evidence_notes.qualifications: Line 30 notes H's complaint was more than 30 days after the written STC report and more than 80 days after the oral verdict. Line 54 records authorship and full-SJC amendment. Line 56 gives a roll-call heading, but the supplied excerpt contains no vote entries.
evidence_notes.incorporated_decisions: None. The PC2 report and Presbytery action at lines 32–34 are the challenged lower-court action quoted for history, not an incorporated decision adopted by the SJC.

source_limits: The source is a short excerpt (pp. 107–109) lacking the full record, the text of BCO 43-2, roll-call vote entries, and any merits analysis of Presbytery's action. It does not state what effect, if any, the not-in-order ruling had on Presbytery's annulment.
